It contrasts recognition with recall and shows why immediate correction prevents repeated errors.","objectives":["Explain the difference between recognition and recall","Design a short feedback loop","Identify delayed-feedback risks"],"keyIdeas":[{"heading":"Recall beats recognition","explanation":"Trying to retrieve an idea reveals whether it is actually available to memory.","example":"Close the notes and explain the concept aloud.","watchOut":"Rereading can feel fluent without producing recall.","evidenceQuote":"test what you can bring back without looking"}],"flashcards":[{"front":"What does active recall test?","back":"Whether an idea can be retrieved without the source in view.","concept":"Active recall"},{"front":"Why should feedback be immediate?","back":"It corrects an error before the wrong pattern is repeated.","concept":"Feedback timing"}],"quiz":[{"question":"Which activity best tests recall?","options":["Rereading a paragraph","Explaining it with the page closed","Highlighting a sentence","Watching it again"],"answerIndex":1,"explanation":"Closing the source removes recognition cues and requires retrieval.","concept":"Active recall"}],"actions":[{"text":"Write three recall questions for the lesson","dueHint":"Today"}],"roadmap":[{"title":"Spaced repetition","why":"It schedules later retrieval after the first feedback loop.","minutes":15}],"cheatSheet":{"headline":"Retrieve, check, correct, and repeat later.","essentials":["Recognition is not recall","Fast feedback prevents repeated errors"],"workflow":["Study one idea","Close the source","Retrieve","Check and correct"],"traps":["Mistaking familiarity for mastery"]},"suggestedQuestions":["Why can rereading feel effective?","How short should a feedback loop be?"]}

The lesson says rereading can create familiarity without proving recall. Its suggested check is to close the source, retrieve the idea in your own words, then compare and correct it. [Source: lesson transcript]
